content.thinking:
I'm planning out the module structure, setting up imports for Three.js, the builder, math/rng utilities, texture and paint helpers, and toon/glow kits, then sketching the bookshelf dimensions before writing the full generator function.

Mapping out the five shelf compartments between boards, assigning content to each row: tall tomes at the bottom, then books with a scroll rack, orbs and candles in the middle, more books and scrolls above, and small items up top, with a crown featuring candles and a large orb at the very top.

I'm writing a helper function to place books along a shelf row—randomizing width, height, and depth, then building each as a colored cover box with a lighter inset "pages" box on the front face, working out how the spine orientation should face outward versus where the pages should sit relative to the shelf depth.

Working out the book geometry...

I'm thinking books can mostly use flat colors or shared cel paint for efficiency despite the quantity. For leaning books, I'm working out how to tilt a composite box around its bottom corner by offsetting the center position based on height and width trig, since rotating a multi-part object precisely is tricky without a grouping mechanism.

Rather than solving the tilt math exactly, I decide to simplify by using horizontal book stacks instead — flat lying boxes built from a bottom board, top board, pages block, and a spine piece positioned along one edge, which is easier to construct and still reads visually as a book. For scrolls, I'm placing them as cylinders lying on their side using a 90-degree rotation.

Refining the lathe outline for the urn...

For the orbs, I'm planning glow spheres with a gold cup base, an inner bright core, and a thin gold torus ring orbiting around, plus maybe tiny floating motes nearby for sparkle.

For candles, I'm sketching wax cylinders with drip spheres, a brass dish holder with handle, and layered flame shapes using elongated glowing spheres in amber tones.

For the frame, I'm adding side panels with a wood grain texture in deep purple-brown tones using a cel-shaded paint approach.

Now I'm switching to a midnight-blue lacquered wood with gold trim for the fantasy aesthetic, applying grain texture along different axes for side panels versus shelves, and planning a back panel decal — a starry sky with gold constellations and arcane circles rendered as an SVG texture behind the books.

For the side panels, I'm adding gold filigree vine decals on outward-facing planes, carefully handling mirroring since the right side faces the opposite direction. Then I'm sketching out a crown piece for the top — a pointed arch shape extruded for dimension.

Shaping arch outline points...

Finial brings total height to about 2.68m, reasonable scale for a tall wizard's bookcase. I'm adding gold-capped corner finials at the top corners, gold trim boxes along the front shelf edges and side panels, and a darker base plinth with a gold accent line sitting flush on the floor.

I need to adjust the plinth height to 0.1 and set the bottom board thickness to 0.02 so it sits cleanly at y=0.11, topping out at 0.12. For decoration, I'll keep it to thematic objects like tomes, scrolls, orbs, candles, and maybe a small crystal cluster, skipping things like cobwebs or skulls to keep it tasteful.

I'll add a hourglass prop on row 4 made of two cones and connecting rods, plus a ring of keys nearby. On the floor I'll add a cluster of melting candles with wax drips and a dish at x=0.8, and a stack of large tomes with a scroll on top at x=-0.85 for extra floor dressing, keeping the whole model within x bounds of ±1.1.

I'm setting up a seeded random generator and defining a palette of book cover colors with a shaded cel function, flat page and gold tones, and caching the rendered book parts for reuse. Writing a helper function to generate rows of books...

Now I'm laying out each shelf row explicitly, deciding book positions, widths, heights, and depths, with gaps for decorative elements like a scroll urn.

Placing scroll pigeonholes around x=0.35: scroll rods extend along z with parchment-spiral decal caps facing forward, rendered as small textured circles. Arranging a pyramid stack of scroll ends, bottom row of four spaced about 0.06 apart starting near x=0.20.

For row2 I'm placing a pedestal orb, a candle cluster, and an hourglass with another orb, spacing them loosely since the back panel fills the gaps. Then I'm starting row3's layout with books positioned toward the left side.

For this section I'm designing a flat open book lying on a small lectern, with cover and page boxes, a gold gem, a glowing rune texture on the pages, and a floating mote above it, plus nearby candle and books to fill out the row before moving to the next shelf level.

For row4 I'm placing small books, a glowing crystal cluster built from cones, a candle, and a stack of flat books, checking their x-positions don't overlap. Then for the top shelf surface I'm starting with a big orb on a gold stand positioned behind the crown.

Now I'm positioning the top shelf items: the orb centered near the crown apex with candelabras flanking at ±0.4, a stack of tomes with a candle on top at -0.45, and a scroll bundle at 0.45, making sure the orb sits below the crown's finial height. Then I'm defining a reusable candle-building helper that creates a wax rod with a darker wax pool disc on top.

Adding flame and drip details...

For the holder I'm adding a gold dish with a ring handle, plus tiny sparkle motes for atmosphere. Now I'm planning the textures: an SVG back panel with a navy gradient background, gold star constellations, a crescent moon, and an arcane circle motif.

Writing filigree vine SVG...

For the rune, I'm sketching a glowing book-spine glyph in viewBox 0 0 16 24 with cyan stroke on transparent background, scaled to size 128 with a circle, vertical line, and diamond shape, meant to overlay book spines as a tinted plane. For the spiral end, I'm drawing a parchment-colored disc with a spiral stroke path in a 32x32 viewBox, using warm gold and brown tones.

Now I'm adding the magic circle rune for the open-book glow effect, a symmetric cyan circle in a 64x64 viewBox scaled to size 256, meant to float as a plane just above the open book. I'm working out the plane orientation so it faces upward correctly, picking an up-vector that keeps the circle properly aligned rather than degenerate.

Next I'm skipping card and star decorations, but adding gold trim details to the shelf fronts - a thin gold box along the shelf edge, plus small ruby gem spheres at the shelf's front center, while skipping corbel brackets and scalloped drops for simplicity. I'm calculating the inner shelf width and starting on the side panel box dimensions.

Now I'm working out the plinth, side panel, and top board heights and positions, settling on a top surface at y=2.15 with sides running from y=0.1 to 2.10, and beginning to lay out the shelf top y-coordinates.

Then I'm computing compartment clearances between each shelf row, adjusting maxH values per row (0.38, 0.36, 0.34, 0.34, 0.24) to fit the urn and orb-on-pedestal objects within the available space.

Now I'm placing the back panel: a painted wood box at z=-0.17 sized to the shelf's width and height, with a textured plane layered just in front of it to add surface detail, sized and centered to match the shelf opening, with books allowed to extend up to 0.28 deep.

For front faces I'm checking depth clearances for the side panels, book fronts, shelf boards and trim to make sure nothing clips. Then I'm designing the orb pedestal as a lathed gold cup profile, validating the polygon points are non-self-intersecting, setting pedestal height to 0.07, and positioning the orb center 0.14 above the base with a radius of 0.085.

For the orb itself, I'm sinking it into the cup and adding a thin tilted ring (torus) around it for a decorative accent. I'm keeping the inner core simple rather than layering a gradient texture, and instead adding two small glowing white highlight spheres near the top to fake a shine/sparkle effect, with the overall glow strength kept moderate so colors don't blow out.

Now I'm moving on to designing the hourglass base.

Still working out hourglass dimensions...

Now I'm planning a crystal cluster using spike shapes, varying their tilt directions and lengths slightly for a natural look, with a glowing cyan color.

For the floor props, I'm adding a stack of tomes on the left using flat books of decreasing size, staggering their x-offsets instead of rotating them for a casual pile effect. On the right I'm placing a cluster of thick, drip-laden candles at varying heights sitting in a dish with a flat cream-colored wax puddle underneath.

Writing geometry parameters...

Skipping the bookmark ribbon and wall candles to keep things simple. I'm estimating the part count stays under 1000 triangles with books at roughly 12 tris per box, and keeping the color palette small with flat fills for gold, cream, and flame tones. Now I'm setting up the builder with default rod sides and starting the actual code for the wizard bookshelf.

Defining helper functions...

Adjusting pages to sit slightly recessed within the covers, then adding gold spine bands near top and bottom plus an extra decorative label band for taller books.

Working through z-depth layering so bands sit just in front of the spine, with the label slightly in front of that, and a glowing rune plane positioned a hair further forward on a dark label background, sized to fit within the label's bounds.

Now I'm writing the function that fills a shelf row with books of randomized width, height, and depth, placing each one sequentially until it no longer fits the available space.

Still writing rod geometry...

I'll use a blue-glazed urn with a gold rim torus, built via the lathe helper. I'm designing an orb function with a gold pedestal lathe, a glowing sphere at scaled radius, a ring, highlights, and small glowing motes, scaling the pedestal outline manually by a factor derived from the orb radius since lathe scaling isn't directly supported.

Now I'm shaping the candle flames as small scaled spheres, then designing the candelabra on top with a gold base, stem rod, and curved arms reaching out to hold three candle cups, plus a stack of tomes with a candle on the opposing side for symmetry.

Writing SVG code...

Still writing filigree path...

Writing more SVG icons...

Still planning part placement...

Still placing shelf elements...

Skipping the ribbon band for simplicity, I'll finish assembling the scene, make sure meta is properly exported, and return the root object.
